stem: The Indian Home Rule Society in London was started by–
expl: In February 1905 A.D. at London, Shyamji Krishna Verma established the Indian Home Rule Society. IHRS established nationalist student hosted named as 'India House' (1905-10) to foster radical Indian nationalist thoughts. The aim of this society was to establish self-rule by intimidating the British Government. From here, a monthly journal ‘The Indian Sociologist’ was started in January 1905. Shyamji departed from London for Paris due to over activeness of Government machinery and later to Geneva.

expl: The Ghadar Party was an organization founded by expatriate Indians settled in the United States and Canada in 1913 AD with the aim of securing India’s independence from British rule. Key members included Lala Hardayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, Kartar Singh Sarabha, and Rash Behari Bose. Sohan Singh Bhakna was the fi rst Chairman of the Ghadar Party. The party used to publish ‘Ghadar’ newspaper which was published in Urdu, Punjabi, Gujrati, Hindi etc. language.

stem: Who is regarded as the “Mother of Indian Revolution”:
expl: Bhikaiji Cama was an Indian freedom fi ghter and political activist. She was born to an extremely wealthy Parsi business family. She led the revolutionary movement from America and Europe for India’s freedom. At the International Socialist Congress held at Stuttgart (Germany) in 1907 A.D., she was the fi rst person to hoist Indian Flag on foreign land. She struggled with her full strength for Indian freedom and worked for it residing in Paris. In 1935 A.D. she returned to Mumbai and in August, 1936 A.D. she died. She was popularly known as ‘’Mother of Indian Revolution’’.

Consider the following events and arrange them in chronological order.
I. The foundation of Ghadar Party
II. Chittagong Armoury Raid
III. Set up of the ‘Indian Independence Committee’ at Berlin
IV. Central Assembly Bomb Case
Select the correct answer from the code given below:
Code :
expl: The Ghadar Movement was an early 20th century, international political movement organised by expatriate Indians to overthrow British rule in India. The offi cial date for the birth of the movement has been considered a meeting on 21 April 1913 AD. The Chittagong armoury raid, also known as the Chittagong uprising, was an attempt on 18 April 1930 A.D. to raid the armoury of police and auxiliary forces from the Chittagong armoury in the Bengal Presidency of British India (now in Bangladesh) by armed Indian freedom fi ghters led by Surya Sen. During the World War-I (1914- 1918), an organisation was founded in Germany, called the Berlin Committee. After 1915, it was renamed the Indian Independence Committee. On April 8, 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt hurled two bombs into the chamber of the Central Legislative Assembly, while it was in session.
